items.headline: PHP-FPM request smuggling flaw may let unauthenticated attackers run PHP code (CVE-2026-129289)
items.summary: PHP may not discard unread bytes from an HTTP request body before it reuses a persistent PHP-FPM or LSAPI connection. In PHP-FPM, an unauthenticated attacker can make those bytes form a separate FastCGI request. That request can bypass front-end routing and run attacker-controlled PHP code with the worker's privileges. The record does not report exploitation.
items.importance_rationale: Unauthenticated code execution in widely deployed PHP-FPM, without reported exploitation.
items.detection_coverage_note: Our assessment: compare web-server access logs with PHP-FPM execution logs to find scripts that ran without a matching routed request. The source cites no detection rules.
items.recommended_action: Make patching internet-facing PHP-FPM deployments a priority once fixed builds are confirmed. Until then, consider turning off persistent FastCGI connections between the front-end server and PHP-FPM.
overrides: Global deployment applicability: every region 95%; cross-industry relevance at least 60%
